CI: docs/checks/phase-20-remote-ci-run-22.json contains exactly 49 contexts, all success (50 "status": "success" = 49 jobs + run), job URLs under runs/22, produced by an authenticated Forgejo statuses/runs read that rejects redirects and takes the token from the environment (no credential in evidence), then recorded only after exact configured-matrix equality; .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:1,90-91 gives 24 features x 2 toolchains + contracts-and-package = exactly 49, matching tools/release_delivery.py:55-68. Document-guard activation, attempt 1's only medium, is now runtime-proven: docs/checks/phase-20-document-activation.json records a traced unittest run where executedGuardLines include 348-366 and exclude 347, i.e. the early return did not fire, with observed locals workspace_version = publication.version = receipt.version = 0.2.2 and receipt.sourceCommit = publication.source_commit = 0716cfd. The delivery-guard receipt is now self-describing (source_sha256, command, producerSha256, verifierSha256, exit_code, result) and records a rehash of the retained registry download against archiveSha256/archiveBytes. Residuals are documentation and in-tree-tooling polish, not functionality: tools/test_ci.py:346-347 still returns silently so a future release needs the same ad-hoc tracer, release_delivery.verify still never rehashes the registry download itself, the tag/CI producers remain untracked .local scripts that docs/RELEASE.md does not describe, RELEASE.md's authorization paragraph still names only 0.1.1/0.2.0, README foregrounds 0.1.1/0.2.0 with repo-relative receipt links, and phase-status still calls the final bookkeeping scan "pending" while the executed 09:57 scan goes unreferenced. findings.description: candidate_private_scan.final_bookkeeping_scan is still "pending", but docs/checks/phase-20-delivery-evidence-private.json records an executed, passing scan at 09:57:37 over 1815 git-visible files at sourceSha256 519219d6 and headCommit 42bcbe0 — after every new 09:55 delivery receipt. That receipt is referenced nowhere in phase 20 bookkeeping, and the chunk's declared scope_evidence (lines 4338-4354) still cites the superseded pre-publication scan docs/checks/phase-20-prepush-private.json (09:13:35, 1804 files), which by its own limitation (line 33) does not certify later changes in excluded check/status bookkeeping. The strongest privacy evidence for this chunk is therefore both unrecorded and outside declared scope, while the record understates what was actually executed.
findings.required_fix: Record the executed delivery-evidence scan in phase 20 bookkeeping (replace final_bookkeeping_scan "pending" with status/evidence docs/checks/phase-20-delivery-evidence-private.json and its source/head fingerprints) and add that path to the chunk scope_evidence so the post-evidence scan is the declared, reviewable privacy artifact.

findings.description: The release-document guard still returns silently when the workspace version differs from the recorded publication version, so an in-tree run cannot distinguish "activated and passed" from "skipped". Activation for this release is proven only by an external traced execution (docs/checks/phase-20-document-activation.json, executedGuardLines 348-366 with 347 absent) produced by the untracked .local/strengthen-delivery-evidence.py. The substance is verified, but the next release will again need an ad-hoc tracer rather than tracked machine-evident output.
findings.required_fix: Have the guard report the resolved workspace and publication versions, and fail rather than return when a published_and_verified publication matches the workspace version but the receipt-specific block was not exercised; alternatively assert that the retained published-document-guard receipt records the same version and source commit as phase-status registry_publication.

findings.description: The final guard re-hashes and re-extracts only the two package archives and requires an absolute retainedArchive for them, while the registry receipt stores a repository-relative path (scripts/verify-publication.py:246) that the guard never reads. The retained registry download .local/artifacts/scm-sdk-0.2.2-registry-c908cad8b27863d0.crate was rehashed for this release only by the one-off producer embedded in docs/checks/phase-20-delivery-guard.json:10, not by the tool, so a later re-run of verify() will not reconfirm the published bytes. The CLI path (lines 197-200) also accepts no --source-sha256 and prints no resolved fingerprint, so a standalone run still self-certifies its source binding.
findings.required_fix: Normalize the retainedArchive path convention across scripts/check-package.py and scripts/verify-publication.py, have verify() rehash registry.retainedArchive against registry.archiveSha256/archiveBytes when present, and either require an explicit --source-sha256 or print the fingerprint the CLI resolved.

findings.description: The procedure documents the registry verification command (lines 38-44) but not how the tag receipt, the Forgejo CI receipt or the final delivery guard were produced. Those three steps were executed by untracked .local scripts whose source survives only inside the receipts (docs/checks/release-tag-v0.2.2.json:31, docs/checks/phase-20-remote-ci-run-22.json:376,390, docs/checks/phase-20-delivery-guard.json:10). Provenance is now adequate, but the next delivery cannot be reproduced from the documented procedure.
findings.required_fix: Add the executed tag/CI/delivery-guard command sequence to docs/RELEASE.md (or land the producers as tracked tools under tools/) so the three remote observations have a documented, repeatable path like verify-publication.py.
